title: Tabular/sigmoid calibration hurt on easy breast-cancer data
hypothesis: Wrapping a train-fold estimator in sigmoid (Platt) calibration should improve Brier / ECE when base probabilities are miscalibrated - measure, don't assume.
data: Public sklearn load_breast_cancer only (methodology demo). Cited from tabular-ml-pipeline and model-eval-calibration portfolio slices.
method: Leakage-safe Pipeline + GroupKFold (tabular-ml-pipeline) and/or StratifiedKFold OOF Platt vs isotonic (model-eval-calibration). Compare raw vs calibrated accuracy, Brier, ECE.
result: On this easy, nearly linear public set, raw logistic was already well calibrated. Sigmoid calibration slightly worsened Brier and ECE (e.g. tabular GroupKFold: raw Brier 0.021 / ECE 0.027 -> calibrated Brier 0.025 / ECE 0.048). Same pattern for LogisticRegression in model-eval-calibration (raw ECE 0.0146 -> Platt 0.0448).
failure_reason: Extra calibration hurt on easy data: when the base model is already well calibrated, Platt/isotonic on small folds adds variance and can increase ECE/Brier. Negative result for the 'calibration always helps' assumption - which is why we measure.
notes: RETROSPECTIVE NOTE from tabular-ml-pipeline / model-eval-calibration READMEs - public toy data only; not a clinical or production claim.
